analysis.title: The Weekly Brief (Market Insights, 23 November 2026)
key_insights: High-quality government bonds offer attractive yields consistent with healthy forward returns. History suggests the current starting yield supports strong medium-term returns.
Unexpectedly large government and corporate issuance in 2026 was a key driver of higher government bond yields by intensifying competition for capital.
The surge in energy prices prompted a major reassessment of central bank rate expectations, adding pressure on bond issuers.
JPM expects the pace of upward revisions to AI-related spending and borrowing is unlikely to be repeated next year.
JPM expects the major Western central banks to raise rates only modestly further.
Government bonds are framed as compelling income today and a diversifier if growth disappoints, per the 2027 Investment Outlook.
Risk assets sold off sharply in the week to 20/11: S&P 500 -8.6%, MSCI AC World -8.0%, MSCI EM -8.2%, with Technology -12.5% the weakest sector.
VIX stood at 36 on 20/11 versus 19 a week earlier and 15 at start of year. Global high yield spreads widened 52bps on the week to 395.
Gold fell 8.3% on the week to $3555/oz and is -17.8% YTD, while Brent is at $92/bbl, -3.9% on the week and +51.3% YTD.
Government yields fell on the week: US 10yr 4.92% (-23bps), UK 5.25% (-10bps), Germany 3.30% (-8bps), Japan 2.78% (-8bps), consistent with a flight to quality.
Defensives outperformed: Cons staples -2.1% and Utilities -3.1% versus Technology -12.5% and Materials -9.4%. Value (-6.8%) beat Growth (-9.3%).
Week ahead: flash composite PMIs for Nov (Eurozone prior 51.7, UK 52.9, US 55.9, Japan 52.1) and US Oct PCE price index y/y (prior 3.6%).

sector_views.rationale: Attractive starting yields support forward returns and offer diversification if growth disappoints.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yield fell 23bps on the week amid risk-off, but remains 76bps higher YTD.
Inflation remains elevated across major economies, limiting central bank easing room.
Growth remains solid in the US.
The prior reading is shown ahead of the next print.
Prior reading shown ahead of the flash release Monday.
JPM does not expect aggressive further tightening.

risk_factors: Further heavy government and corporate issuance, including AI-related borrowing, could keep pressure on yields.
Elevated energy prices could force additional central bank rate repricing.
Economic growth disappointing, which bonds would hedge.
Equity and credit risk-off continuing, with VIX at 36 and HY spreads widening.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 36 on 20/11, up from 19 a week earlier, 15 at start of year and 26 a year ago.
Global IG spreads at 100bps (+9 on week) and Global HY at 395bps (+52 on week), signalling credit stress alongside the equity selloff.

theme_stances.evidence: High-quality government bonds therefore offer compelling income today
